summary:
I extended the record's dual-frame minisuperspace to spatial curvature in both frames: k for ours, k̃ for the dual frame, plus a dual comoving-volume ratio v. Sympy derives the Friedmann and acceleration equations, anchored on the FLRW Ricci scalar computed from the metric. All four rows of #1 §6's dictionary hold in density and in pressure, including "closed dual space ⇒ negative ΔN_eff", and the flat limit reproduces #1 §6. I found no error there. ΔN_eff = −3vM̃²k̃C/[(7/8)(π²/15)T_ν0⁴]. Only vM̃²C³ and vM̃²k̃C are physical, so "M̃ = M_P" constrains nothing by itself.

When our space is closed, the record supports k̃ = 0. The slaved block g̃ = g⁻¹ under the x-leaf section condition has flat fibres. So closure gives no negative ΔN_eff; row 10's ΔN_eff survives only as an independent knob. The symmetric reading k̃ = k makes momentum space a 3-sphere that caps momenta at πħC/R. At C = 1 that is excluded. At C ≥ 10³⁰, for λ = l_P the a⁻⁶ term dominates when the CMB scales leave the horizon.

Closure fixes C only as a normalization (a = R/λ, ã = λ/R), not the a⁻⁶ coefficient. With vM̃² = M_P² and λ = l_P, the dual terms are 10⁻¹⁹⁸ of M_P² or smaller after inflation. The closed de Sitter throat is c/H_inf = 2.67×10⁵ l_P, so ã stays at or below 3.75×10⁻⁶ and the self-dual point is never reached. In any closed universe, R = l_P needs ρ ≥ 0.119ρ_P. The e-fold budget since a throat is 63.6–67.1.

At the turnaround ã is exactly at its minimum, λ/R_max ≈ 10⁻⁶⁴–10⁻⁷⁰ for λ = l_P. In the dual frame our curvature acts as negative dual radiation, and that is what stops the conjugate contraction.

Pairing R with Mc gives an aspect ratio of 4/(3π) to 8/3 at any closed turnaround. That is the Friedmann equation at H = 0, ħ cancels, and the pairing misses the chat's area and ratio by 90+ orders. The obituary stands.

I could not write REPORT.md: the harness refuses report files from subagents. This return carries its content.
